name: Y Scale
summary: Changes vertical aim sensitivity only, so up-down speed can differ from left-right.

where.text: Edit your Config (pencil icon). In the mouse aim or motion aim settings, press the "..." for additional options, then adjust Y Scale.

citations.quote: To edit the current Config, press the pencil icon.
Press the "..." for additional options like setting an Aiming Curve, adjusting Y Scale (vertical only sensitivity), and applying aim Quantization.

definition.text: Y Scale is "vertical only sensitivity". It sits with the Aiming Curve and Quantization under the "..." additional options.

plainWords.text: It changes how fast the reticle moves up and down. Left-right speed stays as your Sensitivity sets it.

plainWords.text: Manager sets Y Scale as a percentage. In the guide's screenshots the field reads 100 % under Mouse Aim and 50 % under Motion Aim.

plainWords.text: The guide doesn't give Y Scale's range or default. The screenshot values (100 and 50) are examples, not stated defaults. Check what Manager shows before you change it.

guidance.text: XIM's advice for mouse aim: start with Sensitivity alone, and change other values, such as Y Scale, only if necessary.

citations.quote: Always start with just adjusting Sensitivity. Change other values only if necessary. There is no "right" set of values. It is preference that matches your gaming style.

aimStyles.text: Mostly tracking. Holding on a target through sustained fire means constant vertical correction against recoil. The guide links more vertical sensitivity to recoil control, though through a temporary Smart Action rather than Y Scale.

citations.quote: Press the "..." for additional options like setting an Aiming Curve, adjusting Y Scale (vertical only sensitivity), and applying aim Quantization.
If you prefer simply increasing your vertical aim sensitivity temporarily as a form of recoil control, you use can use a vertical only aim sensitivity modifier action.

aimStyles.reasoning: Y Scale is vertical-only sensitivity. The guide's "Vertical Sensitivity Boost" raises vertical sensitivity temporarily "as a form of recoil control", so vertical speed matters most where recoil does: sustained fire. No source recommends a Y Scale value for any aim style.
aimStyles.caveat: In Destiny 2, Bungie's account policy says using keyboard/mouse adapters to "reduce recoil" "would be a violation", which can lead to escalating actions, including bans. See the Destiny 2 note on Bungie's policy.

confusions.name: Vertical Sensitivity Boost
confusions.note: A recoil technique in the guide: a Modify Aim Sensitivity action (Y Only) that raises vertical sensitivity only while its binding runs. Y Scale is a permanent Config setting.
